guides.title: Stocking Stuffers for Him That Aren't Junk (All Under $30)
guides.intro: Stocking stuffers are where gift-giving goes wrong: novelty socks, gag gadgets, things that end up in a drawer by New Year's. These are small, useful things from makers who build gear to last. Every pick was under $30 when we checked, so you can fill a stocking without filling a landfill.

guides.title: Leather Anniversary Gifts for Him (3rd Anniversary)
guides.intro: Tradition says the third anniversary is leather, which makes your shopping easier: the material is already decided. We kept to pieces he'll use daily, like a belt, a wallet, or a dopp kit, so the gift gets better with age, the same way you two do.

guides.title: Gifts for a Dad Who Lives on Coffee
guides.intro: Some dads have everything except a better cup of coffee. This list runs from a bag of beans to a serious grinder and brewer, so you can match the gift to your budget and to how deep he is into coffee already. Two picks are manufacturer-refurbished units, and we've labeled them clearly.

guides.title: Everyday Carry (EDC) Gifts for Your Boyfriend
guides.intro: Everyday carry, or EDC, is just the stuff a guy keeps in his pockets: wallet, keys, a knife or tool, maybe a pen. Upgrading one of those things is a gift he'll touch every single day. You don't need to know the jargon. Each pick below says plainly who it suits.

guides.title: Gifts for the Guy Who Works With His Hands
guides.intro: He fixes things, builds things, and always seems to need the one tool he doesn't have. These are tools and workwear from makers people trust, from a starter multitool to pants built for real work.

guides.title: Gifts for a Bourbon Guy (That Aren't More Bourbon)
guides.intro: He already has a favorite bottle, so skip the bottle. These are gifts for how he enjoys a drink: a flask for the game, a shaker for the porch, a candle for the den, and a few other things that go with a quiet pour.

best.h1: Best Gifts for a Bourbon Lover in 2026: The Buyer's Shortlist
best.intro: The best gift for a bourbon lover who already has his bottle is the Stanley Classic Easy Fill Wide Mouth Flask 8 oz ($26). It's built for how he actually drinks bourbon: at the game, at the cabin, at the toast. Below are nine gifts for a bourbon lover that aren't more bourbon, ranked by how closely they tie to the drink, price, and how often he'll use them.
takeaways: Our top pick is the Stanley Classic Easy Fill Wide Mouth Flask 8 oz at $26. It's the most direct bourbon gift on the list without being another bottle.
Four of the nine picks are drinkware (flask, shot glasses, shaker set, pitcher), all from Stanley 1913 and all $45 or less.
The cheapest pick is the Leatherman OPNR at $10, which works as a stocking stuffer or add-on.
The splurge is the Taylor Stitch Seafarer Crew Sweater at $178. It's about the setting he drinks in, not the drink itself.
Every link goes straight to the maker, and every price was checked on the date shown. Prices change, so confirm at checkout.
whatis: A gift for a bourbon lover is something that makes the ritual around the drink better: how he carries it, pours it, shares it, and where he sits with it. It's for the guy whose shelf already has a favorite bottle and who doesn't need you guessing at a new one.

It is not another bottle of bourbon. Picking whiskey for a whiskey guy is risky: he has opinions, and a bottle is gone in a few weekends. It's also not novelty bar décor that ends up in a drawer. Every pick here is something he can use on a regular evening or a weekend away.
criteria: Direct (used to carry, pour, or serve a drink) or setting (for the den, porch, or the evening around it).
The merchant's listed price on the date we checked.
Home, on the go, or both.
A rough call on whether it's an every-week item or a special-occasion one.

faq: What is the best gift for a bourbon lover who has everything?
Something for the ritual rather than the bottle. Our top pick is the Stanley Classic Easy Fill Wide Mouth Flask 8 oz at $26.
What can I get a bourbon lover for under $30?
The Leatherman OPNR ($10), the Stanley flask ($26), or the Stanley nesting shot glass set ($26). Prices are as checked on the date shown.
Should I just buy him a bottle of bourbon?
You can, but if he already has a favorite, you're guessing against his taste. A gift for how he drinks lasts longer than a bottle.
How much should I spend on a bourbon gift?
Most picks here are $26 to $68. The sweater at $178 is the one splurge.
What's a good bourbon gift for a guy who likes to host?
The Stanley Happy Hour Cocktail Shaker Set ($40) or the Stay Chill Pitcher ($45). Both are made for serving a group.
Where do these gifts ship from?
Each link goes straight to the maker (Stanley 1913, Leatherman, Buck Mason, Filson, Taylor Stitch, Portland Leather Goods). Shipping and returns are handled by that merchant.

guides.title: Camping Gifts for Him Under $100
guides.intro: Camping gear can get expensive fast, but the best gifts are often the small things he'll pack on every trip. Every pick here was under $100 when we checked, and all of it is built to handle dirt, weather, and a little abuse.

guides.title: Gifts for Your Father-in-Law (Safe, Classy, Under $150)
guides.intro: A father-in-law gift needs to be safe, classy, and impossible to misread. These are classic, well-made pieces under $150 from established brands. They show you put in thought without trying too hard.

guides.title: Cozy Winter Gifts for Him
guides.intro: When it gets cold, the best gifts are the ones he'll wear all season: a heavy sweater, a good flannel, a beanie that goes with everything. These are cozy, well-made layers in easy colors.

guides.title: First Christmas Together: Gifts for a New Boyfriend (Not Too Much)
guides.intro: Your first Christmas together calls for a gift that's thoughtful but not too much. Nothing here is overly personal or overly expensive. These are useful, good-looking things that say "I pay attention" without saying "I've planned our future."
